entities.summary: Bernard Gui, a Limousin Dominican friar, played a pivotal role in the later stages of the Medieval Inquisition as Bishop of Lodève and papal inquisitor. Born in the late 13th century, Gui was appointed as the inquisitor of southern France in 1307, tasked with rooting out heresy. During his tenure, he established a network of informants and conducted numerous trials, earning him a reputation as a ruthless and efficient inquisitor. Despite his brutal methods, Gui's efforts contributed to a significant decline in heresy in southern France, leaving a lasting impact on the region's religious landscape. Gui's legacy is also marked by his involvement in the composition of the 'Liber Formarum' – a collection of inquisition protocols that standardized procedures for the investigation of heresy across the medieval world. This institutionalization of inquisition practices had far-reaching consequences, shaping the trajectory of European religious history and influencing the development of modern inquisitorial systems.
